reason: min_engine is envelope metadata: the server stamps it unconditionally (server/internal/app/detection.go deviceDetectionCatalog always emits {"extension":"0.5.0","bridge":"0.5.0"}) and never validates a min_engine value against content at all, so a catalogue whose declared floor is 9.9.9 is fully publishable. The Rust engine (endpoint/src/detection.rs verify()) refuses to apply any catalogue whose min_engine exceeds its own compiled ENGINE_VERSION (0.5.0), so it is never actually applied by a 0.5.0 engine. This fixture's top-level min_engine field is consumed only by the corpus-replay tests (content itself carries no min_engine field in either schema); the Rust test mirrors verify()'s version comparison and the extension's engineVersionOk() mirrors it too, so JS and Rust agree.
